did_you_know.text: Did you know? All the people gathered "as one" in the square in front of the Water Gate and asked Ezra the scribe to bring the Book of the Law of Moses.
Did you know? Ezra read from the Law from morning until midday, before the men, women, and all who were able to understand and listen.
Did you know? Ezra read from a wooden platform built especially for the reading, and thirteen leaders or assistants stood beside him.
Did you know? After Ezra blessed the Lord, the people answered, "Amen, amen," raised their hands, and bowed down and worshiped the Lord.
Did you know? The Levites did more than read the Law: they read it, explained it, and made its meaning clear so that the people could understand what was being read.

Did you know? Nehemiah, Ezra, and the Levites taught the people that the holiness of the day was not a reason for sadness, but an opportunity to eat, drink, share with those who had nothing, and rejoice.
Did you know? The people rejoiced because they understood what had been explained to them; the chapter emphasizes understanding as a result of learning the Law.
Did you know? As they studied the Law, they found the command that the Israelites should live in booths during the festival in the seventh month.
Did you know? To build the booths, the people were asked to bring branches of olive, oil-bearing trees, myrtle, palm, and leafy trees.

Did you know? The Law was read every day during the seven days of the Festival of Booths, and on the eighth day there was a solemn assembly; the passage also describes great rejoicing and living in booths.
